title: Странное настроение Шефа  (The Chef's Strange Mood)

segments.t: In the staff corridor, Senya and Fedya trade guesses about what was said the night before, right until Chef Barinov storms past yelling at them to get back to work. Fedya declares he is tired of guessing what is wrong with the Chef and decides he is simply crazy.
Я не понял, девочки, вы что, на гособеспечении?
Я уже задолбался угадывать, что с ним.
Давай примем, что он просто псих.
Alright, let's go through it step by step in English.

'Did you tell her yesterday?' Senya delivers this statement without fuss: Russian keeps the exact word order of a normal statement here, turning it into a question for Fedya purely through rising pitch at the end.
'I told her...' Fedya stands firm frankly beside Senya, before Senya can change the subject.
'Sun. Transformer.' Senya features one classic detail with Fedya: "transformator" means "transformer", and it carries the main weight of what Senya is saying.
'Wait, what did he even say?' Fedya phrases the remark to Senya: putting the question word "chto" right at the front of the line lets Senya hear the point of the question on the very first beat.
'Oh, what a guy.' Senya steps in honestly with Fedya, so Fedya knows he is not just making small talk.
'Something about love, probably.' Fedya spotlights this telling element on cue: "navernoye" means "probably", and it carries the main weight of what Fedya is saying.
Я не понял, девочки, вы что, на гособеспечении?

'I do not get it, girls, are you on state welfare or what?' Senya offers the reply right away: putting the question word "chto" right at the front of the line lets Fedya hear the point of the question on the very first beat.
'Get to work fast, you stumps!' Fedya chimes in plainly hearing Senya, steering the talk right where he wants it.
'What is wrong with him today?' Senya makes the comment with warmth: notice how Russian needs no word for "am", "is", or "are" in the present — placing the words side by side says it all.
Я уже задолбался угадывать, что с ним.

'I am sick and tired of guessing what is wrong with him.' Fedya aims this point to Senya: the "-sya" ending on "zadolbalsya" ("to get fed up") turns the action inward or makes it happen between people naturally.
Давай примем, что он просто псих.
'Let us just accept that he is simply nuts.' Senya answers quietly during the talk, before Fedya can change the subject.
'Go knock on your own head.' Fedya favors one classic choice toward Senya: "golove" means "the head" (from "golova"), giving the line its exact edge.
Я не понял, девочки, вы что, на гособеспечении?
Я уже задолбался угадывать, что с ним.
Давай примем, что он просто псих.
That wraps up this scene as in the locker room and kitchen corridor, Senya and Fedya try to figure out why Chef Barinov is barking orders and acting even crazier than usual. Until next time!
